answer: At dawn, an agent offering ocean-current forecasts must first lock a nontransferable bond and receive a ticket bound to its key, epoch, and a random route segment. Validators later request hidden samples from that segment and compare signed sensor records with independent buoys; a mismatched hash or duplicated segment is objective evidence that burns the bond and voids the reward. A raven operator may create many aliases, but n aliases require n bonds, n distinct segments, and n verifiable records. Reusing one ocean sample earns once, so extra names add cost without influence.
